Each independent object is a set of nested, axis-aligned rectangular bands (sometimes the innermost region is a solid block). Keep the object's exact shape, position, and all zero/background cells. Read the colors from the outermost band inward, then reverse that list: recolor the outermost band with the original innermost color, the next band with the next-to-innermost color, etc. For an odd number of bands, the middle band's color stays in the middle. This reversal applies independently to each object.

Demo 1 left object has nested colors outer-to-inner `[8, 7, 4, 3]`; output has `[3, 4, 7, 8]`. Demo 1 right object has `[2, 1, 3]`; output has `[3, 1, 2]`. The geometry and background remain unchanged.

Three separate objects:
- Upper-left nested layers outer-to-inner `[3, 6, 1, 4]` -> `[4, 1, 6, 3]`.
- Upper-right nested layers `[5, 4, 8]` -> `[8, 4, 5]`.
- Lower large nested layers `[6, 8, 2, 4, 3]` -> `[3, 4, 2, 8, 6]`.
The successful submission preserved all original coordinates/background and performed just those per-object color reversals.

When submitting, preserve input dimensions exactly (20 rows x 19 columns here) and ensure every row has 19 cells.
